I study how children and adolescents regulate emotion within family and peer
systems, and how moment-to-moment regulatory dynamics become longer-term
patterns of adaptation and physiological health.

My work pairs physiological measurement — respiratory sinus arrhythmia, dyadic
synchrony, ambulatory heart-rate variability — with intensive longitudinal
designs such as 14-day diaries and experience sampling. Methodologically I work
in within-person dynamics, person-centred models, and network approaches, mostly
in **R** and **Mplus**.

I work with [Aprile Benner](https://liberalarts.utexas.edu/hdfs/) at UT Austin.
Before this I earned an M.A. in Human Development and Family Sciences at UT
Austin, and an M.A. in Developmental Psychology and a B.S. in Psychology at
Beijing Normal University.

I also teach statistics — a [research methods course as instructor of
record](teaching.qmd), graduate SEM and statistics as a TA, and an annual R
workshop series for graduate students in my department.
